subject.title: [Bug]: Clarify Telegram channel_post auth when groups[chatId].allowFrom is configured

question: For Telegram `channel_post` commands from an explicitly allowed chat, should configured `groups[chatId].allowFrom` be ignored because Telegram does not expose the human sender, or should the command fail closed with a clear unsupported-policy message?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the correct behavior is a security/product policy choice because it decides whether channel-level authorization can substitute for sender-scoped authorization.

options.title: Fail Closed With Clear Policy
options.body: When `channel_post` lacks a human sender and a per-group sender allowlist is configured, reject the command and document the unsupported configuration.

options.title: Use Explicit Chat Allow
options.body: Treat explicit `channels.telegram.groups[chatId]` allow as sufficient for channel posts and document that sender-scoped `allowFrom` is ignored on that surface.

options.title: Defer To Bot-To-Bot Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open until a broader Telegram bot-to-bot policy PR defines the permanent channel-post authorization model.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed With Clear Policy
recommendation.body: When `channel_post` lacks a human sender and a per-group sender allowlist is configured, reject the command and document the unsupported configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: Their open Telegram bot-to-bot policy PR is the closest current policy work touching this same channel_post authorization boundary.
